steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper proposing a diffusion-model-based 3D human pose prior (DPoser): why pose priors matter, where existing priors fall short, what diffusion models offer, our approach, and our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Why human pose priors matter and why they are hard
- Limitations of existing pose priors (GMMs, VAEs, NDFs)
- Diffusion models and their current use for human pose/motion
- DPoser and truncated timestep scheduling
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Motivation
  - accurate human pose modeling: fundamental topic; applications from human-robot interaction to AR/VR
  - real-world applications need prior distribution of valid poses: body model fitting, motion capture, gesture recognition
  - complex biomechanics + extensive kinematic variability -> hard to build robust, realistic prior
- Previous priors
  - GMMs, VAEs, Neural Distance Fields (NDFs)
  - GMMs: unbounded -> implausible poses
  - VAEs: Gaussian assumptions -> average poses, miss full spectrum of actions
  - NDFs: promising for 3D surface modeling, struggle to generalize over complex high-dim pose manifolds
  - -> need more comprehensive, dependable approach (this work)
- Diffusion models
  - capture complex high-dim distributions; versatile sampling
  - used for lifelike human motion sequences; multi-hypothesis pose estimators from 2D inputs
  - but designed for specific generation tasks or conditional inputs -> limited applicability
  - potential as universal human pose prior largely untapped; effective optimization for diverse tasks unanswered
- DPoser
  - time-dependent denoiser learned from expansive motion capture datasets -> robust pose prior
  - pose-centric tasks as inverse problems; integrate via variational diffusion sampling as regularization in frameworks like SMPLify
  - pose-related info mostly at latter stages of diffusion trajectory -> truncated timestep scheduling for optimization
  - vs standard uniform scheduling: +5.4% human mesh recovery, +17.2% pose completion, +3.8% motion denoising
- Contributions
  - DPoser: diffusion-based, robust, flexible prior; integration across tasks via test-time optimization
  - analysis of diffusion timesteps in pose domain; truncated scheduling
  - extensive experiments: outperforms SOTA pose priors on downstream tasks

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Modeling human pose accurately is a fundamental research topic, and it can help many applications, from human-robot interaction to augmented and virtual reality experiences. Many real-world applications depend on a prior distribution of valid human poses to do tasks like body model fitting, motion capture, and gesture recognition. Human biomechanics is complex and there is a lot of kinematic variability in how people move, so it is a big challenge to build a human pose prior that is robust and realistic.

Earlier work on human pose priors has mostly used techniques like Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and Neural Distance Fields (NDFs). But each of these has its own limitations. GMMs can generate implausible poses because they are unbounded. VAEs are restricted by their Gaussian assumptions, so they tend to generate average poses that may not capture the full spectrum of human actions. NDFs have shown promise for 3D surface modeling but have trouble generalizing over the complex, high-dimensional landscape of human pose manifolds. So there is a pressing need for a more comprehensive and dependable way to model human pose priors, and this is what this work tries to do.

- diffusion models: gaining traction; capture complex high-dim distributions, versatile sampling
  - lifelike human motion sequences; multi-hypothesis pose estimators from 2D inputs
  - but specific generation tasks / conditional input -> limited; universal prior untapped, optimization unanswered
- DPoser: time-dependent denoiser from expansive mocap datasets
  - inverse problems; variational diffusion sampling as regularization in SMPLify-like frameworks
  - pose info at latter stages -> truncated timestep scheduling; beats uniform by 5.4%, 17.2%, 3.8% (mesh recovery, pose completion, motion denoising)
- contributions (3 bullets)

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Modeling human pose accurately is a fundamental research topic, and it can help many applications, from human-robot interaction to augmented and virtual reality experiences. Many real-world applications depend on a prior distribution of valid human poses to do tasks like body model fitting, motion capture, and gesture recognition. Human biomechanics is complex and there is a lot of kinematic variability in how people move, so it is a big challenge to build a human pose prior that is robust and realistic.

Earlier work on human pose priors has mostly used techniques like Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and Neural Distance Fields (NDFs). But each of these has its own limitations. GMMs can generate implausible poses because they are unbounded. VAEs are restricted by their Gaussian assumptions, so they tend to generate average poses that may not capture the full spectrum of human actions. NDFs have shown promise for 3D surface modeling but have trouble generalizing over the complex, high-dimensional landscape of human pose manifolds. So there is a pressing need for a more comprehensive and dependable way to model human pose priors, and this is what this work tries to do.

Recently, diffusion models have become popular because they are good at capturing complex, high-dimensional data distributions and they allow versatile sampling techniques. They have been used to generate lifelike human motion sequences and as multi-hypothesis pose estimators from 2D inputs. But these models are made for specific generation tasks or for conditional input data, and this limits how they can be applied more broadly. Using diffusion models as a universal human pose prior is still largely untapped, and how to do effective optimization for diverse tasks is still not answered.

In this work we propose DPoser, a new approach that uses a time-dependent denoiser learned from expansive motion capture datasets to build a robust human pose prior. We treat various pose-centric tasks as inverse problems and propose to integrate DPoser through variational diffusion sampling techniques as a regularization component inside optimization frameworks like SMPLify. We also found that significant pose-related information during diffusion is mostly located at the latter stages of the diffusion trajectory. This led us to develop a new truncated timestep scheduling strategy for optimization. It outperforms the standard uniform scheduling, with gains of 5.4%, 17.2%, and 3.8% in human mesh recovery, pose completion, and motion denoising, respectively.

Our main contributions are:

- We introduce DPoser, a new framework based on diffusion models for a robust and flexible human pose prior, which can be integrated into diverse pose-related tasks through test-time optimization.

- We analyze how diffusion timesteps affect the pose domain and propose truncated scheduling for more efficient optimization.

- With extensive experiments, we show that DPoser is better than state-of-the-art (SOTA) pose priors in a variety of downstream tasks.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Accurate modeling of human pose is a fundamental research topic that can benefit various applications, from human-robot interaction to augmented and virtual reality experiences. Many real-world applications rely on a prior distribution of valid human poses to perform tasks like body model fitting, motion capture, and gesture recognition. The complexity of human biomechanics, together with the extensive kinematic variability in movement patterns, makes constructing a robust and realistic human pose prior a significant challenge.

Previous efforts to model human pose prior have mainly employed techniques such as Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) [1], Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) [2], and Neural Distance Fields (NDFs) [3]. Each technique, however, has its own limitations. GMMs, for instance, might generate implausible poses due to their unbounded nature. VAEs, restricted by their Gaussian assumptions, tend to generate average poses that may not capture the full spectrum of human actions. NDFs have shown promise in 3D surface modeling but struggle to generalize across the complex, high-dimensional landscape of human pose manifolds. These limitations highlight a pressing need for a more comprehensive and dependable approach to modeling human pose priors, which this work seeks to address.

Recently, Diffusion models [4,5,6,7] have gained traction for their ability to capture complex, high-dimensional data distributions and to enable versatile sampling techniques. They have been applied to generating lifelike human motion sequences [8,9] and as multi-hypothesis pose estimators from 2D inputs [10,11]. However, these models are designed for specific generation tasks or tailored to conditional input data, which limits their applicability in broader contexts. The potential of diffusion models as a universal human pose prior remains largely untapped, and the question of effective optimization methods for diverse tasks remains unanswered.

In this work, we propose DPoser, a novel approach that leverages a time-dependent denoiser learned from expansive motion capture datasets to construct a robust human pose prior. We regard various pose-centric tasks as inverse problems and suggest integrating DPoser via variational diffusion sampling techniques [12] as a regularization component within optimization frameworks like SMPLify [1]. Furthermore, our investigations show that significant pose-related information during diffusion is predominantly located at the latter stages of the diffusion trajectory. This inspired us to develop a novel truncated timestep scheduling strategy for optimization, which outperforms the standard uniform scheduling with gains of 5.4%, 17.2%, and 3.8% in human mesh recovery, pose completion, and motion denoising, respectively.

In summary, our main contributions are as follows:

- • We introduce DPoser, a novel framework based on diffusion models to craft a robust and flexible human pose prior, designed for seamless integration across diverse pose-related tasks via test-time optimization.

- • We analyze the impact of diffusion timesteps in the pose domain and propose truncated scheduling for more efficient optimization.

- • Through extensive experiments, we establish that DPoser outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) pose priors in a variety of downstream tasks.
